audit_status.source_base: Hebrew source via Sefaria with source/English versification reconciliation; public-domain KJV familiar comparison
audit_status.review_note: Drafted a source-centered English rendering of 2 Chronicles 16 (14 verses, KJV numbering). YHWH rendered for יהוה; preserved prophetic rebuke, diplomatic payments, military action, and Asa’s illness and burial. Minor witness issues flagged for later review.

verses.restored: In the thirty-sixth year of Asa king of Judah, Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah and built Ramah, to prevent any going out or coming in to Asa king of Judah.

familiar.text: In the six and thirtieth year of the reign of Asa Baasha king of Israel came up against Judah, and built Ramah, to the intent that he might let none go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Ramah as a blocking fortress for access to Asa.

modern.text: In the thirty-sixth year of Asa’s reign, Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah and fortified Ramah to prevent anyone from leaving or entering the territory of Asa king of Judah.

original.text: בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וָשֵׁשׁ֙ לְמַלְכ֣וּת אָסָ֔א עָלָ֞ה בַּעְשָׁ֤א מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ עַל יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיִּ֖בֶן אֶת הָרָמָ֑ה לְבִלְתִּ֗י תֵּ֚ת יוֹצֵ֣א וָבָ֔א לְאָסָ֖א מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה

verses.restored: Then Asa took silver and gold from the treasuries of the house of YHWH and from the king’s house, and sent it to Ben‑Hadad king of Aram who lived in Damascus, saying,

familiar.text: Then Asa brought out silver and gold out of the treasures of the house of the LORD and of the king’s house, and sent to Benhadad king of Syria, that dwelt at Damascus, saying,

notes.title: short
notes.body: House of YHWH (בֵּית יְהוָֹה) distinguished from the king’s house.

modern.text: So Asa withdrew the silver and gold from the treasuries of the house of the LORD and the royal palace, and he sent it with this message to Ben-hadad king of Aram, who was ruling in Damascus:

original.text: וַיֹּצֵ֨א אָסָ֜א כֶּ֣סֶף וְזָהָ֗ב מֵאֹֽצְר֛וֹת בֵּ֥ית יְהוָ֖ה וּבֵ֣ית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיִּשְׁלַ֗ח אֶל בֶּן הֲדַד֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֔ם הַיּוֹשֵׁ֥ב בְּדַרְמֶ֖שֶׂק לֵאמֹֽר

verses.restored: ‘There is a league between me and you, as between my father and your father. Behold, I have sent you silver and gold; go, break your league with Baasha king of Israel, that he may depart from me.’

familiar.text: There is a league between me and thee, as there was between my father and thy father: behold, I have sent thee silver and gold; go, break thy league with Baasha king of Israel, that he may depart from me.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Asa appeals to ancestral treaty and uses treasure to induce rupture.

modern.text: “Let there be a treaty between me and you, between my father and your father. See, I have sent you silver and gold. Now go and break your treaty with Baasha king of Israel, so that he will withdraw from me.”

original.text: בְּרִית֙ בֵּינִ֣י וּבֵינֶ֔ךָ וּבֵ֥ין אָבִ֖י וּבֵ֣ין אָבִ֑יךָ הִנֵּ֨ה שָׁלַ֤חְתִּֽי לְךָ֙ כֶּ֣סֶף וְזָהָ֔ב לֵ֞ךְ הָפֵ֣ר בְּרִֽיתְךָ֗ אֶת בַּעְשָׁא֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְיַעֲלֶ֖ה מֵעָלָֽי

verses.restored: And Ben‑Hadad listened to King Asa, and sent the captains of his host against the cities of Israel; they struck Ijon, Dan, Abel‑maim, and all the store‑cities of Naphtali.

familiar.text: And Benhadad hearkened unto king Asa, and sent the captains of his armies against the cities of Israel; and they smote Ijon, and Dan, and Abelmaim, and all the store cities of Naphtali.

notes.title: short
notes.body: List of northern towns attacked; 'store‑cities' implies logistics/depots.

modern.text: And Ben-hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Israel, conquering Ijon, Dan, Abel-maim, and all the store cities of Naphtali.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֨ע בֶּן הֲדַ֜ד אֶל הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אָסָ֗א וַ֠יִּשְׁלַח אֶת שָׂרֵ֨י הַחֲיָלִ֤ים אֲשֶׁר לוֹ֙ אֶל עָרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיַּכּוּ֙ אֶת עִיּ֣וֹן וְאֶת דָּ֔ן וְאֵ֖ת אָבֵ֣ל מָ֑יִם וְאֵ֥ת כָּֽל מִסְכְּנ֖וֹת עָרֵ֥י נַפְתָּלִֽי

verses.restored: When Baasha heard of it he ceased building Ramah and stopped his work.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when Baasha heard it, that he left off building of Ramah, and let his work cease.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Baasha abandons construction once northern pressure occurs.

modern.text: When Baasha learned of this, he stopped fortifying Ramah and abandoned his work.

original.text: וַיְהִי֙ כִּשְׁמֹ֣עַ בַּעְשָׁ֔א וַיֶּחְדַּ֕ל מִבְּנ֖וֹת אֶת הָרָמָ֑ה וַיַּשְׁבֵּ֖ת אֶת מְלַאכְתּֽוֹ

verses.restored: Then Asa the king took all Judah; they carried away the stones of Ramah and its timber which Baasha had been using, and built with them Geba and Mizpah.

familiar.text: Then Asa the king took all Judah; and they carried away the stones of Ramah, and the timber thereof, wherewith Baasha was building; and he built therewith Geba and Mizpah.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Material re‑used for Geba and Mizpah; communal labor implied.

modern.text: Then King Asa brought all the men of Judah, and they carried away the stones of Ramah and the timbers Baasha had used for building. And with these materials he built up Geba and Mizpah. Hanani’s Message to Asa

original.text: וְאָסָ֣א הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ לָקַח֙ אֶת כָּל יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיִּשְׂא֞וּ אֶת אַבְנֵ֤י הָֽרָמָה֙ וְאֶת עֵצֶ֔יהָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּנָ֖ה בַּעְשָׁ֑א וַיִּ֣בֶן בָּהֶ֔ם אֶת גֶּ֖בַע וְאֶת הַמִּצְפָּֽה

verses.restored: At that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah and said to him, ‘Because you relied on the king of Aram and did not rely on YHWH your God, the army of the king of Aram escaped from your hand.

familiar.text: And at that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah, and said unto him, Because thou hast relied on the king of Syria, and not relied on the LORD thy God, therefore is the host of the king of Syria escaped out of thine hand.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Hanani reproves Asa for political reliance instead of reliance on YHWH.

modern.text: At that time Hanani the seer came to King Asa of Judah and told him, “Because you have relied on the king of Aram and not on the LORD your God, the army of the king of Aram has escaped from your hand.

original.text: וּבָעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא בָּ֚א חֲנָ֣נִי הָרֹאֶ֔ה אֶל אָסָ֖א מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו בְּהִשָּׁ֨עֶנְךָ֜ עַל מֶ֤לֶךְ אֲרָם֙ וְלֹ֤א נִשְׁעַ֨נְתָּ֙ עַל יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ עַל כֵּ֗ן נִמְלַ֛ט חֵ֥יל מֶֽלֶךְ אֲרָ֖ם מִיָּדֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Were not the Cushites and the Lubim a great host, with very many chariots and horsemen? Yet because you relied on YHWH, he delivered them into your hand.

familiar.text: Were not the Ethiopians and the Lubims a huge host, with very many chariots and horsemen? yet, because thou didst rely on the LORD, he delivered them into thine hand.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Cush and Lubim (foreign powers) cited as examples of previous deliverance by trust in YHWH.

modern.text: Were not the Cushites and Libyans a vast army with many chariots and horsemen? Yet because you relied on the LORD, He delivered them into your hand.

original.text: הֲלֹ֧א הַכּוּשִׁ֣ים וְהַלּוּבִ֗ים הָי֨וּ לְחַ֧יִל לָרֹ֛ב לְרֶ֥כֶב וּלְפָרָשִׁ֖ים לְהַרְבֵּ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד וּבְהִשָּֽׁעֶנְךָ֥ עַל יְהוָ֖ה נְתָנָ֥ם בְּיָדֶֽךָ

verses.restored: For the eyes of YHWH run to and fro throughout the whole earth to show himself strong on behalf of those whose heart is perfect toward him. You have acted foolishly in this; therefore from now on you shall have wars.

familiar.text: For the eyes of the LORD run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to shew himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him. Herein thou hast done foolishly: therefore from henceforth thou shalt have wars.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Sovereign observation tied to the moral condition of the heart; prophetic consequence pronounced.

modern.text: For the eyes of the LORD roam to and fro over all the earth, to show Himself strong on behalf of those whose hearts are fully devoted to Him. You have acted foolishly in this matter. From now on, therefore, you will be at war.”

original.text: כִּ֣י יְהוָ֗ה עֵינָ֞יו מְשֹׁטְט֤וֹת בְּכָל הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ לְ֠הִתְחַזֵּק עִם לְבָבָ֥ם שָׁלֵ֛ם אֵלָ֖יו נִסְכַּ֣לְתָּ עַל זֹ֑את כִּ֣י מֵעַ֔תָּה יֵ֥שׁ עִמְּךָ֖ מִלְחָמֽוֹת

verses.restored: Then Asa was angry with the seer, and put him in the prison house; for he was in a rage with him because of this. And Asa oppressed some of the people at that time.

familiar.text: Then Asa was wroth with the seer, and put him in a prison house; for he was in a rage with him because of this thing. And Asa oppressed some of the people the same time.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Punitive response to prophetic speech; oppression recorded without justification.

modern.text: Asa was angry with the seer and became so enraged over this matter that he put the man in prison. And at the same time Asa oppressed some of the people. The Death and Burial of Asa

original.text: וַיִּכְעַ֨ס אָסָ֜א אֶל הָרֹאֶ֗ה וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֨הוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית הַמַּהְפֶּ֔כֶת כִּֽי בְזַ֥עַף עִמּ֖וֹ עַל זֹ֑את וַיְרַצֵּ֥ץ אָסָ֛א מִן הָעָ֖ם בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִֽיא

verses.restored: Behold, the acts of Asa, first and last, are written on the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.

familiar.text: And, behold, the acts of Asa, first and last, lo, they are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Reference to royal annals as fuller source.

modern.text: Now the rest of the acts of Asa, from beginning to end, are indeed written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.

original.text: וְהִנֵּה֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י אָסָ֔א הָרִאשׁוֹנִ֖ים וְהָאַחֲרוֹנִ֑ים הִנָּ֤ם כְּתוּבִים֙ עַל סֵ֣פֶר הַמְּלָכִ֔ים לִיהוּדָ֖ה וְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: In the thirty-ninth year of his reign Asa became diseased in his feet, and his disease was severe; yet in his disease he did not seek YHWH, but the physicians.

familiar.text: And Asa in the thirty and ninth year of his reign was diseased in his feet, until his disease was exceeding great: yet in his disease he sought not to the LORD, but to the physicians.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Hebrew indicates reliance on physicians rather than seeking YHWH in the illness.

modern.text: In the thirty-ninth year of his reign, Asa became diseased in his feet, and his malady became increasingly severe. Yet even in his illness he did not seek the LORD, but only the physicians.

original.text: וַיֶּחֱלֶ֣א אָסָ֡א בִּשְׁנַת֩ שְׁלוֹשִׁ֨ים וָתֵ֤שַׁע לְמַלְכוּתוֹ֙ בְּרַגְלָ֔יו עַד לְמַ֖עְלָה חָלְי֑וֹ וְגַם בְּחָלְיוֹ֙ לֹא דָרַ֣שׁ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֖י בָּרֹפְאִֽים

verses.restored: Then Asa rested with his fathers and died in the one and fortieth year of his reign.

familiar.text: And Asa slept with his fathers, and died in the one and fortieth year of his reign.

modern.text: So in the forty-first year of his reign, Asa died and rested with his fathers.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֥ב אָסָ֖א עִם אֲבֹתָ֑יו וַיָּ֕מָת בִּשְׁנַ֛ת אַרְבָּעִ֥ים וְאַחַ֖ת לְמָלְכֽוֹ

verses.restored: They buried him in his own tomb which he had prepared in the city of David, and laid him in the bed that was filled with spices and varied ointments, and they made a very great burning for him.

familiar.text: And they buried him in his own sepulchres, which he had made for himself in the city of David, and laid him in the bed which was filled with sweet odours and divers kinds of spices prepared by the apothecaries’ art: and they made a very great burning for him.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Burial with spices and a large pyre; ritual details retained from the Hebrew.

modern.text: And he was buried in the tomb that he had cut out for himself in the City of David. They laid him on a bier that was full of spices and various blended perfumes; then they made a great fire in his honor.

original.text: וַיִּקְבְּרֻ֣הוּ בְקִבְרֹתָ֗יו אֲשֶׁ֣ר כָּֽרָה לוֹ֮ בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִיד֒ וַיַּשְׁכִּיבֻ֗הוּ בַּמִּשְׁכָּב֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר מִלֵּא֙ בְּשָׂמִ֣ים וּזְנִ֔ים מְרֻקָּחִ֖ים בְּמִרְקַ֣חַת מַעֲשֶׂ֑ה וַיִּשְׂרְפוּ ל֥וֹ שְׂרֵפָ֖ה גְּדוֹלָ֥ה עַד לִמְאֹֽד

translation_notes: Rendered chiefly from the supplied Hebrew lines; KJV verse numbering preserved for output.
Divine name יהוה rendered as YHWH. Kept diplomatic bribery, prophetic censure, and medical detail literal and ambiguous where the Hebrew is.
Mystical_translation provides a contemplative, non-lexical companion distinct from the restored draft.
safety_note: Contains violence, coerced labor and burial rites; preserved for historical fidelity—do not use for incitement or justification of harm.
